clue.text: Clots ordered catalogues

indicators.note: put in order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone orders catalogues and is called a clot for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clots' looks like a plural noun (fools), but it is the verb: blood clots, that is, coagulates.
explanation.definitionFit: To clot is to thicken into lumps, which is to coagulate.

clue.text: Regularly clubbish, helpful youngsters

indicators.note: take letters at regular intervals: the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th

explanation.surface: Young people who go clubbing regularly are nonetheless described as helpful.
explanation.walkthrough: Cubs are the junior Scouts, whose motto is to do a good turn, hence 'helpful'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cub Scouts are youngsters known for doing good deeds.

clue.text: Lie next to some comma butterflies

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following words are used

explanation.surface: Something lies beside a group of comma butterflies.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma is a real British butterfly, named for a white comma-shaped mark on its wing, so the surface reads naturally.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that abut lie directly next to each other.

clue.text: C. Asian beatniks bizarrely getting into action-film staple

indicators.note: getting into means entering, so the rearranged letters go inside the gun

parts.note: the Uzi submachine gun is a fixture of action films

indicators.note: bizarrely means in a strange way, so the letters of beatniks are jumbled

explanation.surface: Central Asian beat-generation types turn up oddly in a gun-heavy thriller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'C.' is the usual short form of Central. The Uzi is an Israeli submachine gun, a familiar prop in action films.
explanation.definitionFit: An Uzbekistani is a native of Uzbekistan, a Central Asian republic, so the word works as an adjective for the region.

clue.text: Becoming upset: concession and alternative put before old man

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the column upside down, so it reads backwards
the first two parts come ahead of the third

parts.note: a sop is a concession made to placate someone

explanation.surface: Someone grows upset at a compromise offered ahead of their father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Becoming upset' reads as one phrase about getting cross; split it, and 'Becoming' is the definition while 'upset' tells you to reverse SOPORPA.
explanation.definitionFit: Becoming can mean fitting or suitable, which is what apropos means.

clue.text: Heartlessly acquiring grasping Romeo's jewelry

parts.note: R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet, placed inside EAR…ING

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted person gets their hands on Romeo's jewels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Acquiring' has to be swapped for EARNING before the heart comes out; losing the middle of 'acquiring' itself leads nowhere.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: an earring is one kind of jewelry, and the singular answer fits the mass noun as one item of it.

clue.text: Dairy product moulded, recalled

indicators.note: called back, so the word runs backwards

explanation.surface: A moulded dairy product has been recalled from the shops.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheese really is moulded and really is recalled, which is why 'moulded' passes as a description of the product rather than the word to reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by category: cheese is made from milk, and the Dutch round with a red wax rind is one example.

clue.text: Ignored (like some consumer goods after Christmas)

definitions.text: like some consumer goods after Christmas
definitions.meaning: the post-Christmas sales, where prices are cut

explanation.surface: Something is ignored, rather like goods left over after the Christmas rush.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is the January sales: goods are discounted, sold at reduced prices.
explanation.definitionFit: To discount an idea is to disregard it; discounted goods are marked down.

clue.text: Everyman's enjoyment? Don't worry about it

definitions.meaning: the setter's own delight, spoken in the first person
the polite brush-off to someone thanking you

explanation.surface: The setter enjoys the work and waves away the solver's thanks.
explanation.walkthrough: Everyman is the setter, so from his own mouth his enjoyment is MY PLEASURE; the question mark flags that self-reference.
explanation.definitionFit: 'My pleasure' is a polite reply to thanks, meaning think nothing of it.

clue.text: Fat old queen finally consoles those clearly upset

indicators.note: 'finally' means at the end, so only the end of 'consoles' is wanted: its last letter

explanation.surface: An overweight former monarch comforts people in visible distress.
explanation.walkthrough: To blubber is to cry noisily, so blubberers are people whose upset is plain to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Blubberers are people weeping openly, clearly upset.

clue.text: Acronym soliciting alacrity, primarily (using initial letters)?

definitions.text: Acronym soliciting alacrity, primarily (using initial letters)?

indicators.note: the bracket tells us to take the first letter of each of the four words before it

parts.note: the opening letters of these words are A, S, A and P

explanation.surface: A dictionary-style gloss describing a short form that urges speed, built from first letters.
explanation.walkthrough: The four words' initials spell the answer, and the whole clue describes it: an acronym asking for speed.
explanation.definitionFit: ASAP stands for 'as soon as possible', an abbreviation used to demand prompt action.

clue.text: Giving Hitchcock film a miss; it prompts you to jump

definitions.meaning: first reading, taken literally: giving a film a miss is skipping it, and the Hitchcock thriller here is the 1948 film Rope
second meaning: the playground toy swung under the feet that you hop over

explanation.surface: Someone passes up a Hitchcock screening, which spurs them into action.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads as 'skipping Rope', Rope being a Hitchcock film. 'prompts you to jump' sounds like a fright, as in a thriller, but means making you hop.
explanation.definitionFit: A skipping rope is swung over the head and under the feet, so each turn calls for a hop.

clue.text: Gorge shape formed with river — studied by these?

definitions.note: the definition is a hint: gorges and their shapes are what these people study

indicators.note: the letters are formed into a new word

explanation.surface: A gorge carved by a river is something specialists would study.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes a landform, so the answer turns back on it: the people who study gorges and rivers are geographers.
explanation.definitionFit: Geographers study landforms such as gorges shaped by rivers.

clue.text: Bikram, so Amy mostly contorted with hands on hips

indicators.note: contorted means twisted out of shape, so these letters are rearranged
mostly means most of the word, so the last letter of Amy goes

explanation.surface: In a Bikram hot yoga class, Amy twists herself into a pose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims AMY to AM, and 'contorted' rearranges BIKRAM, SO and AM. Bikram is a style of hot yoga, which suits the contortions.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing arms akimbo means having the hands on the hips with elbows turned outwards.

clue.text: Bets glasses will be filled with last of Cointreau after hours

indicators.note: the glasses take the other pieces inside them, as if filled

parts.note: specs is informal for spectacles, glasses

indicators.note: only the final letter of Cointreau is used

parts.note: late means after the usual hours

explanation.surface: Someone's drinks are topped up with orange liqueur at a late-night bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'glasses' looks like drinking vessels but here means spectacles; U and LATE go inside SPEC_S.
explanation.definitionFit: To speculate is to gamble or take a risk on a possible gain, as one does when placing a wager.

clue.text: Once again asks for some moments of peace?

explanation.surface: Someone repeats a request for a bit of quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as RE-POSES the word means 'asks again'; read as one word, reposes are rests, spells of calm.
explanation.definitionFit: Repose is rest or tranquillity, so reposes are moments of peace.

clue.text: Coffee leftovers in the gardens and so on

definitions.meaning: the spent powder left after brewing
the land around a big house: lawns, gardens, park

explanation.surface: Used coffee is being tipped into the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Coffee grounds really are spread on gardens as compost, which glues the two meanings into one scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Grounds are both the dregs of coffee and the gardens and land around a building.

clue.text: Gatherings seen in Instagram, Facebook, &c.

explanation.surface: Party photos turn up on social media.
explanation.walkthrough: A social is an informal party; 'socials' is also current slang for social-media accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: Socials are social gatherings and, informally, social-media platforms.

clue.text: Stinger's tail's removed: it's a sign

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its last letter, and here it is taken away

parts.note: a scorpion is a stinger, an animal with a sting in its tail

explanation.surface: An insect's sting has been taken out, which is a sign of something.
explanation.walkthrough: A scorpion's sting really is in its tail, so the surface invites a literal reading; here the tail is the word's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorpio is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac, the Scorpion, covering late October to November.

clue.text: Artist showing Royal Marines (instead of Navy) in façade

indicators.note: one piece takes the place of another, so the navy letter is replaced
showing means putting on display, so the marines are put on view in the façade

parts.note: a veneer is a façade, a superficial outward show

explanation.surface: A painter depicts marines rather than sailors on the front of a building.
explanation.walkthrough: In VENEER, swap the N for RM.
explanation.definitionFit: Johannes Vermeer was the Dutch painter of Girl with a Pearl Earring, a Golden Age master.

clue.text: Empty-headedness in post

definitions.meaning: a vacant, thoughtless state of mind

explanation.surface: A vacant person has landed a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is only a link; the two meanings are vacuity of mind and an unfilled job.
explanation.definitionFit: Vacancy means lack of thought, and also an open position.

clue.text: Those in prang manage OK, we're told, in series of unpredictable events

indicators.note: we hear it said, so the spelling follows the sound

parts.note: those in a prang (a minor car crash) are colliders; cope = manage all right

explanation.surface: People in a car crash get by, apparently, amid a run of chaotic events.
explanation.walkthrough: A prang is British slang for a minor car crash, so those in it are colliders. Said together, 'colliders cope' sounds like KALEIDOSCOPE.
explanation.definitionFit: A kaleidoscope, figuratively, is a constantly shifting pattern or sequence of things.

clue.text: In short, endless cheese

indicators.note: endless means without its end, so the final letter is cut off

parts.note: in short means brief, concisely put

explanation.surface: To summarise: a cheese that goes on forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In short' looks like a link phrase meaning 'to sum up', but it gives BRIEF.
explanation.definitionFit: Brie is a soft, creamy French cheese with a white rind, named after its home region.

clue.text: Name of lad that's trapped in rotisserie

indicators.note: the answer is caught inside the next word

explanation.surface: A boy has got stuck in a spit-roasting oven.
explanation.walkthrough: A rotisserie is a rotating spit for roasting meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: 'name of lad' asks for any boy's first name, and Otis, as in Otis Redding, is one.

clue.text: Small child's great power reported

indicators.note: said aloud, so we go by the sound

explanation.surface: A little child is said to have enormous strength.
explanation.walkthrough: A mite is an affectionate word for a tiny child.
explanation.definitionFit: A mite is literally a tiny creature, and by extension an affectionate word for a very small child, as in 'poor little mite'.

clue.text: Love writes on Greek island — fifth of sonnets moving — don't we know it!

indicators.note: on means coming next, so the writing word follows the love letter

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
to pen is to write, so pens means writes

indicators.note: fifth of means the fifth letter of the following word

parts.note: the fifth letter of sonnets is E

indicators.note: moving means shifting position, so the matching letter leaves its place in the island and goes ahead of it

parts.note: Crete is the largest Greek island

explanation.surface: A lover writes poems on a Greek island, with everyone smugly aware of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' says the E is shifted: the last E of CRETE moves to the front, giving ECRET. 'don't we know it!' is a clue for something everyone already knows.
explanation.definitionFit: An open secret is supposedly confidential but in fact widely known, which is what the exclamation implies.

clue.text: Topple American in overtime

indicators.note: the first part goes inside the second

explanation.surface: An American toppled during extra time of a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topple' is a verb here, as in topple a government, and so is OUST.
explanation.definitionFit: To oust someone is to remove or topple them from power.

clue.text: … poser prancing with style in artificial fabrics

indicators.note: leaping about, so the letters move

explanation.surface: A show-off prances about stylishly in synthetic clothes, following on from the clue before.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading dots continue the previous clue's surface; they play no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: polyester is a plastic spun into thread, so its cloths are man-made rather than natural.
